s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological condition with worsening symptoms over time, primarily affecting one side of the body, with comorbid mental health symptoms
salient_findings: Difficulty on the left side of the body
key_facts: Comorbid symptoms of depression and anxiety
Main difficulties noted on the left side of the body
Brain MRI in 2013 showed brain aging and partially empty sella turcica
Follow-up Brain MRI in 2020 showed mild cerebral atrophy and micro-ischemic focal lesions

shortlist.label: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological condition with worsening symptoms over time, primarily affecting one side of the body

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Comorbid symptoms of depression and anxiety, and brain MRI findings of micro-ischemic focal lesions

shortlist.label: Primary Lateral Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Initial presentation with leg pain and progressive worsening of symptoms

shortlist.label: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia
shortlist.why_kept: Family history not provided, but condition could explain progressive neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Asymmetric neurological symptoms and presence of micro-ischemic focal lesions on brain MRI

raw.rationale: The patient's initial presentation with leg pain, progressive worsening of symptoms, and main difficulties noted on one side of the body are consistent with Primary Lateral Sclerosis. The absence of specific physical examination findings and the presence of comorbid depression and anxiety also align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
rejected.why: ALS typically presents with both upper and lower motor neuron signs, which are not mentioned in the case report.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: MS typically presents with optic neuritis, sensory symptoms, or brainstem symptoms, which are not mentioned in the case report.

rejected.label: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia
rejected.why: HSP is a genetic disorder, and there is no mention of a family history or genetic testing in the case report.

rejected.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
rejected.why: CBD typically presents with a combination of motor and cognitive symptoms, and the patient's MMSE scores do not indicate significant cognitive decline.
